10	## Functional requirements

18	- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
19	- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
20	- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
21	- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.

34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.

52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;

56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]

76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |

88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.

96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. 103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.

14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Token:
26	    kind: str
27	    raw: str
28	    value: str | int | float | None
29	    start: int
30	    end: int
31	    line: int
32	    column: int

35	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
36	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
37	
38	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
39	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
40	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
41	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
42	    """
43	    tokens = []
44	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
45	
46	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
47	        nonlocal i, line, column
48	        text = sql[i:end]
49	        newlines = text.count("\n")
50	        if newlines:
51	            line += newlines
52	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
53	        else:
54	            column += end - i
55	        i = end
56	
57	    while i < len(sql):
58	        char = sql[i]
59	        if char in " \t\r\n":
60	            advance(i + 1)
61	            continue
62	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
63	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
64	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
65	            continue
66	
67	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
68	        if char in "\"'":
69	            quote = char
70	            end = i + 1
71	            decoded = []
72	            while end < len(sql):
73	                if sql[end] == quote:
74	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
75	                        decoded.append(quote)
76	                        end += 2
77	                        continue
78	                    end += 1
79	                    break
80	                decoded.append(sql[end])
81	                end += 1
82	            else:
83	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
84	                               else "quoted identifier")
85	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
86	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
87	            value = "".join(decoded)
88	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
89	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
90	        ):
91	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
92	            end = match.end()
93	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
94	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
95	            raw = match.group()
96	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
97	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
98	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
99	            end = match.end()
100	            raw = match.group()
101	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
102	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
103	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
104	            end = i + 2
105	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
106	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
107	            end = i + 1
108	            kind = value = char
109	        else:
110	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
111	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
112	                            token_line, token_column))
113	        advance(end)
114	
115	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
116	    return tokens

13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.

29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.

35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.

49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.

1	# minisql: Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- Stack: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- Package location: `minisql/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`), with `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`.
7	- Entry points: `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` from repo root; `import minisql; minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
8	- Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser.
9	
10	## Functional requirements
11	
12	- **R1** Importable as `minisql`, runnable as `python -m minisql`; standard-library imports only, never `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser.
13	- **R2** Tables load from the data directory per the data contract.
14	- **R3** Column types are inferred per the inference rules; empty fields are NULL.
15	- **R4** The tokenizer implements the lexical rules.
16	- **R5** The parser implements the grammar and precedence table.
17	- **R6** Keywords and all names resolve case-insensitively.
18	- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
19	- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
20	- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
21	- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.
22	- **R11** INNER and LEFT joins follow nested-loop semantics and order.
23	- **R12** Grouping, `HAVING` and aggregates follow the aggregate rules, including empty input.
24	- **R13** `DISTINCT` keeps first occurrences.
25	- **R14** `ORDER BY` supports aliases, ordinals, expressions, multiple keys, `ASC`/`DESC`; NULLs smallest; stable ties.
26	- **R15** `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take non-negative integer literals.
27	- **R16** Clauses evaluate in the defined order; `AND`/`OR` short-circuit.
28	- **R17** The library API matches the contract.
29	- **R18** CSV and table formats match byte-for-byte.
30	- **R19** The one-shot CLI follows the output and exit-code rules.
31	- **R20** The REPL follows the prompt, buffering, command and exit rules.
32	- **R21** Errors use the specified classes, format, templates and positions.
33	
34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
44	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.
45	
46	### Grammar (EBNF)
47	
48	```
49	query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
50	            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
51	            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
54	item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
55	tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
63	                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
64	cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
65	add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
66	mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
67	unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
68	primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
69	call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
70	colref    = name ["." name] ;
71	name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
72	```
73	
74	`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.
75	
76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |
87	
88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference

3	from __future__ import annotations

5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re

9	from .model import parse_integer

12	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
13	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
14	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
15	)
16	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
17	_NUMBER = re.compile(
18	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
19	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
20	)
21	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Token:
26	    kind: str
27	    raw: str
28	    value: str | int | float | None
29	    start: int
30	    end: int
31	    line: int
32	    column: int
33	
34	
35	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
36	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
37	
38	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
39	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
40	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
41	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
42	    """
43	    tokens = []
44	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
45	
46	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
47	        nonlocal i, line, column
48	        text = sql[i:end]
49	        newlines = text.count("\n")
50	        if newlines:
51	            line += newlines
52	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
53	        else:
54	            column += end - i
55	        i = end
56	
57	    while i < len(sql):
58	        char = sql[i]
59	        if char in " \t\r\n":
60	            advance(i + 1)
61	            continue
62	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
63	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
64	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
65	            continue
66	
67	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
68	        if char in "\"'":
69	            quote = char
70	            end = i + 1
71	            decoded = []
72	            while end < len(sql):
73	                if sql[end] == quote:
74	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
75	                        decoded.append(quote)
76	                        end += 2
77	                        continue
78	                    end += 1
79	                    break
80	                decoded.append(sql[end])
81	                end += 1
82	            else:
83	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
84	                               else "quoted identifier")
85	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
86	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
87	            value = "".join(decoded)
88	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
89	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
90	        ):
91	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
92	            end = match.end()
93	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
94	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
95	            raw = match.group()
96	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
97	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else parse_integer(raw)
98	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
99	            end = match.end()
100	            raw = match.group()
101	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
102	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
103	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
104	            end = i + 2
105	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
106	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
107	            end = i + 1
108	            kind = value = char
109	        else:
110	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
111	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
112	                            token_line, token_column))
113	        advance(end)
114	
115	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
116	    return tokens

13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.

29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.

35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.

49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.
